classification.habit: Perennial erect shrub, 1–2.5 m tall, with bluntly quadrangular stems.
classification.habitat: Forests and moist shady places, especially along forest edges.
classification.distribution: Throughout India, particularly the Himalayan foothills, Eastern India and the Western Ghats.

identification.description: Shrub with bluntly quadrangular stems, opposite or ternate serrate leaves, terminal panicles of pale blue-violet flowers and succulent purple-black drupes.
identification.whole_plant: Erect shrub with whorled serrate leaves and terminal panicles of pale blue to violet flowers.
identification.root: Hard, woody, cylindrical, up to 5 cm thick, light brown with elongated lenticels; bark thin and easily separated; wood with marked medullary rays and concentric rings; taste acrid.
identification.stem: Bluntly quadrangular, little branched, with prominent leaf scars.
identification.leaf: Opposite or in whorls of three, subsessile, elliptic-oblong, 10–25 cm long, coarsely serrate.
identification.flower: Pale blue to violet, in terminal panicles; the lower corolla lobe larger and deep blue; stamens long-exserted.
identification.fruit: Drupe, 4-lobed, black-purple when ripe, seated on the enlarged persistent calyx.
identification_points: Woody root with thin, easily separable bark
Prominent medullary rays and growth rings
Whorled serrate leaves and blue-violet flowers

therapeutics.precautions: Ushna and may aggravate Pitta in excess; use with care in bleeding tendencies. Authenticate the root, as other species are sold as Bharangi.
therapeutics.contraindications: Avoid in Pitta-predominant conditions and in pregnancy without advice.

modern_information.safety_notes: Generally well tolerated at classical doses; data on long-term use and pregnancy are limited.
